title: Attestation, submission and filing lifecycle never rewrite history
summary: Above a sealed snapshot, Accounting Core can freeze who asserted approval, under which authority/key identity, what exact report/attestation set was submitted, and the regulator/workflow observations that followed. A correction produces a new filing with exact predecessor lineage; it never rewrites the original report or receipt.
invariants: An attestation binds the exact snapshot/boundary plus attestor, asserted authority identity, proof/key identities and evidence.
Accounting records asserted authority but does not decide whether the actor legally possessed that authority; external authority/security/legal layers decide that.
Submission evidence freezes the exact snapshot and attestation set plus external submission/receipt identities.
ORIGINAL, AMENDMENT and CORRECTION filing versions bind exact predecessor fingerprints where applicable.
Lifecycle observations are append-only: SUBMITTED, RESUBMITTED, ACKNOWLEDGED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, WITHDRAWN and SUPERSEDED.
A later backdated journal may make the old snapshot REPORT_POPULATION_STALE while the old signature and receipt remain valid evidence of what was actually approved/filed.
Withdrawal, rejection and supersession never delete or mutate the historical submission evidence.

provenance.claim: Attestation/submission evidence binds exact snapshot, asserted authority/key identities and exact submission evidence without deciding legal authority.
Filing versions and workflow observations are append-only; corrections/supersession never rewrite historical reports, signatures or receipts.
